_meta.description: Concept2Cure proprietary Comprehensive ICH Guidelines Database — all ICH guidelines with detailed requirements, CTD mapping, and regulatory impact analysis.

Q1A_R2.title: Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products
Q1A_R2.scope: Long-term, accelerated, and intermediate stability testing conditions and requirements
keyRequirements: Intermediate: 30°C±2°C / 65%RH±5%RH (triggered if significant change at accelerated)
Minimum 3 batches of drug substance and drug product
Shelf life extrapolation: maximum 2x available long-term data

Q1B.title: Stability Testing: Photostability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products
keyRequirements: Expose to ≥1.2 million lux hours visible + ≥200 W·h/m² UV
Sequential design: drug substance → drug product → drug product in container
If protected from light needed, demonstrate container closure protection

Q1C.title: Stability Testing for New Dosage Forms
Q1C.scope: Reduced stability data package for new dosage forms of already approved drug substances

Q1D.title: Bracketing and Matrixing Designs for Stability Testing
keyRequirements: Bracketing: testing only extremes of design factors (e.g., strength, container size)

Q1E.title: Evaluation for Stability Data
keyRequirements: Statistical analysis approaches for shelf life determination

Q1F.title: Stability Data Package for Registration Applications in Climatic Zones III and IV
Q1F.note: Replaced by WHO guidelines for zones III/IV. Individual agencies define local conditions.

Q2_R2.title: Validation of Analytical Procedures
keyRequirements: Specificity, linearity, range, accuracy, precision (repeatability + intermediate)
NEW in R2: Lifecycle approach to analytical procedure management
NEW in R2: Analytical Target Profile (ATP) concept
NEW in R2: Enhanced change management and continuous verification

Q3A_R2.title: Impurities in New Drug Substances
keyRequirements: Structure elucidation for impurities above identification threshold
Qualification via safety studies or literature for impurities above qualification threshold

Q3B_R2.title: Impurities in New Drug Products
keyRequirements: Max daily dose ≤1mg: reporting 1.0%, identification 1.0%, qualification 1.0%
Max daily dose 1mg-10mg: reporting 0.5%, identification 0.5%, qualification 1.0%
Max daily dose >10mg-2g: reporting 0.2%, identification 0.2%, qualification 0.5%
Max daily dose >2g: reporting 0.1%, identification 0.1%, qualification 0.2%

Q3C_R8.title: Residual Solvents
keyRequirements: Class 1 solvents: AVOID (carcinogenic) — benzene, carbon tetrachloride, etc.
Class 2 solvents: LIMIT — acetonitrile ≤410ppm, methanol ≤3000ppm, DCM ≤600ppm, etc.
Class 3 solvents: LOW risk — ≤5000ppm (e.g., acetone, ethanol, ethyl acetate)

Q3D_R2.title: Elemental Impurities
keyRequirements: Class 1 (Cd, Pb, As, Hg): Always evaluated — human toxicants with limited/no use
Class 2A (Co, Ni, V): Evaluated for all routes — high probability of occurrence
Class 2B (Ag, Au, Ir, Os, Pd, Pt, Rh, Ru, Se, Tl): Evaluated based on process
Class 3 (Ba, Cr, Cu, Li, Mo, Sb, Sn): Low toxicity, oral PDE ≥500μg/day
Risk assessment approach: identify, evaluate, control, review

Q3E.title: Extractables and Leachables
keyRequirements: Risk-based approach for container closure and manufacturing equipment
Analytical Evaluation Threshold (AET) based on Safety Concern Threshold
Applies to packaging, delivery devices, manufacturing equipment
Correlation of extractables to leachables required

Q5A_R2.title: Viral Safety Evaluation of Biotechnology Products Derived from Cell Lines of Human or Animal Origin
keyRequirements: Cell line characterization for adventitious viruses
Viral clearance validation studies (minimum 2 orthogonal steps)
Log reduction values (LRV) for model viruses
NEW in R2: Updated for modern analytical methods, NGS for virus detection

Q5B_R1.title: Analysis of the Expression Construct in Cells Used for Production of r-DNA Derived Protein Products

Q5D.title: Derivation and Characterisation of Cell Substrates
keyRequirements: Cell bank system: Master Cell Bank (MCB) and Working Cell Bank (WCB)
Identity, purity, stability of cell banks

Q5E.title: Comparability of Biotechnological/Biological Products Subject to Changes in Their Manufacturing Process
keyRequirements: Non-clinical and clinical comparability may be needed depending on significance of change
Risk-based approach to evaluating process changes

Q6A.title: Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria for New Drug Substances and New Drug Products: Chemical Substances
keyRequirements: Universal tests: appearance, identity, assay, impurities
Specific tests: dissolution, hardness, friability, water content, etc.
Decision trees for setting acceptance criteria
Justification based on manufacturing, stability, clinical experience

Q6B.title: Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria for Biotechnological/Biological Products

Q7.title: Good Manufacturing Practice Guide for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients
keyRequirements: Impurity control strategy from starting material onward
Applies from defined starting material to final API

Q8_R2.title: Pharmaceutical Development
keyRequirements: Links to process understanding and lifecycle management

Q9_R1.title: Quality Risk Management
keyRequirements: Risk assessment tools: FMEA, FTA, HACCP, PHA
Risk identification → analysis → evaluation → control → review → communication
NEW in R1: Formality of QRM based on risk level
NEW in R1: Caution against subjectivity and bias in risk assessments
NEW in R1: Risk-based decision making must be science-based

Q10.title: Pharmaceutical Quality System
keyRequirements: Continual improvement of process performance and product quality
Lifecycle stages: development → technology transfer → manufacturing → discontinuation

Q11.title: Development and Manufacture of Drug Substances (Chemical Entities and Biotechnological/Biological Entities)
keyRequirements: Design space for drug substance manufacturing
Control strategy linking to drug substance CQAs

Q12.title: Technical and Regulatory Considerations for Pharmaceutical Product Lifecycle Management
keyRequirements: Established Conditions (ECs): what requires regulatory notification
Categorization of changes and reporting requirements

Q13.title: Continuous Manufacturing of Drug Substances and Drug Products
keyRequirements: Process validation approaches specific to CM

Q14.title: Analytical Procedure Development
keyRequirements: Minimal vs enhanced approach to development

S1A_R1.title: Regulatory Need for Carcinogenicity Studies of Pharmaceuticals
keyRequirements: Required for drugs administered ≥6 months continuously
Required for drugs with cause for concern (genotoxicity, structure-activity)
Waived for unequivocally genotoxic compounds (already classified as carcinogens)

S1B_R1.title: Testing for Carcinogenicity of Pharmaceuticals
keyRequirements: NEW R1: Weight-of-evidence (WoE) assessment may reduce need for 2-year bioassay
Integrative approach: genotoxicity, chronic tox, pharmacology, clinical data
Rasopathy models (Tg.rasH2) as alternatives to traditional 2-year studies
Reduces animal use where scientifically justified

S2_R1.title: Genotoxicity Testing and Data Interpretation for Pharmaceuticals Intended for Human Use
keyRequirements: Standard battery: Ames test (bacterial reverse mutation) + in vitro chromosomal aberration/micronucleus + in vivo test
Option 1: Ames + in vitro MN (human lymphocytes or mammalian cells) + in vivo MN
Option 2: Ames + in vivo MN (with 2 tissue exposure assessment)
Follow-up strategies for positive in vitro results

S3A.title: Note for Guidance on Toxicokinetics
S3A.scope: Assessment of systemic exposure in toxicology studies

S3B.title: Pharmacokinetics: Guidance for Repeated Dose Tissue Distribution Studies

S4.title: Duration of Chronic Toxicity Testing in Animals (Rodent and Non-Rodent Toxicity Testing)
keyRequirements: Rodent: 6 months for drugs indicated ≥6 months
Non-rodent: 9 months for drugs indicated ≥6 months
Species selection: one rodent + one non-rodent (usually rat + dog or monkey)

S5_R3.title: Detection of Toxicity to Reproduction for Human Pharmaceuticals
keyRequirements: Fertility and early embryonic development (Segment I)
Integration of male fertility with general toxicity studies possible

S6_R1.title: Preclinical Safety Evaluation of Biotechnology-Derived Pharmaceuticals
keyRequirements: Species selection based on pharmacological relevance
In vitro tissue cross-reactivity studies for monoclonal antibodies

S7A.title: Safety Pharmacology Studies for Human Pharmaceuticals
keyRequirements: hERG assay for QT prolongation risk
Supplemental studies: renal, GI, other organ systems

S7B_R1.title: Nonclinical Evaluation of the Potential for Delayed Ventricular Repolarization (QT Interval Prolongation)
keyRequirements: In vivo QT study in non-rodent species
NEW R1: Best practices, integrated risk assessment with E14

S8.title: Immunotoxicity Studies for Human Pharmaceuticals
keyRequirements: Standard toxicity studies can provide initial immunotoxicity data
Additional studies (T-cell dependent antibody response) if WoE indicates concern

S9.title: Nonclinical Evaluation for Anticancer Pharmaceuticals
keyRequirements: Reduced nonclinical package for advanced cancer indications
Genotoxicity: Ames test sufficient for initial FIH
Chronic toxicity may not be needed for advanced cancer

S10.title: Photosafety Evaluation of Pharmaceuticals
keyRequirements: In vivo study only if in vitro equivocal

S11.title: Nonclinical Safety Testing in Support of Development of Paediatric Medicines
keyRequirements: Integration with existing adult toxicology data
Study design considerations for developing organisms

S12.title: Nonclinical Biodistribution Considerations for Gene Therapy Products
keyRequirements: Biodistribution study design for gene therapy vectors
Integration with pharmacokinetics of gene therapy products

E1.title: The Extent of Population Exposure to Assess Clinical Safety
keyRequirements: Minimum 1500 patients exposed for non-life-threatening conditions
At least 300-600 for 6 months, 100 for 12 months
Safety database requirements scale with indication severity

E2A.title: Clinical Safety Data Management: Definitions and Standards for Expedited Reporting
keyRequirements: Definitions: adverse event, adverse drug reaction, unexpected ADR, serious AE
Serious: death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly

E2B_R3.title: Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) — Electronic Transmission
keyRequirements: E2B(R3) message structure and data elements
Gateway compatibility: EudraVigilance, FDA FAERS, PMDA

E2C_R2.title: Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER)
keyRequirements: International birth date (IBD) and data lock point (DLP)

E2D.title: Post-Approval Safety Data Management
E2D.scope: Post-marketing safety reporting standards and responsibilities

E2E.title: Pharmacovigilance Planning
keyRequirements: Safety specification: important identified/potential risks, missing information

E3.title: Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports
keyRequirements: Safety tables and narratives for SAEs/deaths

E4.title: Dose-Response Information to Support Drug Registration
E4.scope: Design and conduct of dose-response studies

E5_R1.title: Ethnic Factors in the Acceptability of Foreign Clinical Data
keyRequirements: Intrinsic and extrinsic ethnic factors assessment
Bridging study design when foreign data extrapolation not justified
Critical for PMDA submissions (Japanese bridging requirement)

E6_R2_R3.title: Good Clinical Practice
keyRequirements: NEW R3 Annex 1: Proportionate approaches to trial management
NEW R3 Annex 2: Use of technological innovations and decentralized trials

E7.title: Studies in Support of Special Populations: Geriatrics
keyRequirements: Minimum geriatric patient representation in database

E8_R1.title: General Considerations for Clinical Studies
keyRequirements: Quality by Design (QbD) for clinical trials
NEW R1: Modernized clinical trial design concepts

E9_R1.title: Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials
keyRequirements: NEW R1: Estimand framework — population, variable, intercurrent events, summary measure
Strategies for intercurrent events: treatment policy, composite, hypothetical, principal stratum, while on treatment

E10.title: Choice of Control Group and Related Issues in Clinical Trials
E10.scope: Guidance on placebo control, active control, no-treatment control, dose-response control

E11_R1.title: Clinical Investigation of Medicinal Products in the Paediatric Population
keyRequirements: Extrapolation of efficacy from adults to pediatric

E12.title: Clinical Evaluation by Therapeutic Category (multiple guidelines)
E12.scope: Therapeutic area-specific guidance for cardiovascular, oncology, etc.

E14_R3.title: Clinical Evaluation of QT/QTc Interval Prolongation and Proarrhythmic Potential for Non-Antiarrhythmic Drugs
keyRequirements: Thorough QT (TQT) study design or concentration-QT analysis
NEW R3: C-QTc modeling can replace standalone TQT study
Integration with S7B in vitro hERG data

E15.title: Definitions for Genomic Biomarkers, Pharmacogenomics, Pharmacogenetics, Genomic Data and Sample Coding Categories
E15.scope: Harmonized terminology for genomics in drug development

E16.title: Biomarkers Related to Drug or Biotechnology Product Development: Context of Use

E17.title: General Principles for Planning and Design of Multi-Regional Clinical Trials
keyRequirements: Sample size considerations for multi-regional consistency
Evaluation of treatment effect consistency across regions
Regulatory acceptance of MRCT data across ICH regions
Statistical methods for regional subgroup analysis

E18.title: Genomic Sampling and Management of Genomic Data
E18.scope: Collection, storage, and use of genomic samples and data in clinical trials

E19.title: Optimization of Safety Data Collection
keyRequirements: Reduced burden of AE collection where scientifically justified
Prespecified events of interest vs comprehensive AE capture
Applicable to certain late-stage and post-approval studies

E20.title: Adaptive Clinical Trials
keyRequirements: Regulatory communication requirements for adaptive designs

M1.title: CTD Module 1 — Administrative Information and Prescribing Information
M1.scope: Each region has own Module 1 specifications (FDA, EMA, PMDA, etc.)

M2.title: CTD Module 2 — Common Technical Document Summaries

M3_R2.title: Nonclinical Safety Studies for the Conduct of Human Clinical Trials and Marketing Authorization
keyRequirements: Timing of nonclinical studies relative to clinical development phase
Phase I requirements: GLP tox (2 species), genotoxicity (Ames + in vitro), safety pharmacology core battery
Phase II requirements: repeat-dose tox ≥ clinical duration
Phase III requirements: chronic tox, repro tox, carcinogenicity assessment

M4_R4.title: Common Technical Document (CTD) Organisation
keyRequirements: Module 2: Summaries (QOS, nonclinical overview, clinical overview)

M4_Q_R1.title: CTD — Quality (M4Q R1)
keyRequirements: 3.2.S: Drug Substance (nomenclature, manufacture, characterization, control, standards, container, stability)
3.2.P: Drug Product (description, composition, development, manufacture, control, standards, container, stability)

M4_S.title: CTD — Safety (M4S)
keyRequirements: 4.2.1: Pharmacology (primary PD, secondary PD, safety pharmacology)
4.2.3: Toxicology (single dose, repeat dose, genotox, carcinogenicity, repro tox, local tolerance)

M4_E.title: CTD — Efficacy (M4E)
keyRequirements: 5.3.5: Efficacy and safety studies (controlled, uncontrolled, analyses)
5.3.7: Case report forms and individual patient listings

M5.title: eCTD — Data Elements and Message Specification
M5.scope: Technical specification for electronic CTD submission
keyRequirements: PDF technical requirements for leaf documents

M7_R2.title: Assessment and Control of DNA Reactive (Mutagenic) Impurities in Pharmaceuticals to Limit Potential Carcinogenic Risk
keyRequirements: Compound-specific risk assessment for known mutagens
In silico (QSAR) assessment: two complementary methods (expert rule + statistical)
Class 1-5 classification system for mutagenic impurities
Less-than-Lifetime (LTL) exposure limits for clinical trials
Purge factor analysis for process control

M8.title: eCTD v4.0
M8.scope: Next-generation electronic submission standard using HL7 RPS

M9.title: Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS)-Based Biowaivers
keyRequirements: BCS Class I: High solubility, high permeability — biowaiver eligible
BCS Class III: High solubility, low permeability — biowaiver eligible (with rapid dissolution)
Dissolution testing: 85% in ≤30 minutes (BCS I) or ≤15 minutes (BCS III)

M10.title: Bioanalytical Method Validation and Study Sample Analysis
keyRequirements: Full validation parameters: selectivity, LLOQ, calibration curve, accuracy, precision, matrix effect, carryover, stability
Incurred sample reanalysis (ISR): ≥67% within ±20% for small molecules, ±30% for large molecules

M11.title: Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP)
keyRequirements: Structured data elements for machine-readable protocols
Alignment with TransCelerate Common Protocol Template

M12.title: Drug Interaction Studies
keyRequirements: In vitro DDI evaluation: CYP enzymes, transporters
PBPK modeling for DDI prediction and dose adjustment
Labeling recommendations based on DDI data

M13A.title: Bioequivalence for Immediate-Release Solid Oral Dosage Forms
keyRequirements: Crossover and parallel BE study designs
Acceptance criteria: 80-125% (90% CI for geometric mean ratio)
Narrow therapeutic index drugs: tightened criteria
